label: token g read in the original phase
explanation: Token detector for the letter g in the original (pre-<DEL>) input. It fires on every g in the original phase (dev precision 1.0, recall 0.9997) and on no other token. Magnitude is highest for a g at t=0 (1.0 of max) and drops for g later in the sequence (about 0.3-0.6 at t=5-8). It is also lower for a repeated g than for the first occurrence (e.g. 0.67, 0.33). It does not fire on the <DEL> step, and it essentially never fires on g fed back in the copy phase: the only exceptions are 36 near-zero activations (0.00-0.02) at recall_idx 1 when the sequence starts with g.

issues: No refutation found. Test split: precision 1.0, recall 0.99965, F1 0.99982, mass recall 0.999993. Misses: 0 false positives. The 38 missed activations are all near zero (0.00-0.05 of max) on g fed back at recall_idx 1, in sequences where g is original token 0 and L=3. Together they carry 0.0% of the activation mass, which matches the explanation's stated exception.

Phase claims hold. Dev: 108108 activations in the original phase, 0 at the delimiter, 36 in the copy phase. 54% of g inputs are active overall. Since the predicate has precision 1, every original-phase g fires.
The magnitude claim holds. t=0 is 15.5% of active steps but 21.0% of activation mass, and mass share falls with t faster than count does.

The repeated-g claim holds. Requiring a first occurrence (n_seen([tok('g')])==0) gives test recall 0.909, as stated. Repeated g's are 9.1% of active steps but only 6.9% of mass, so they fire more weakly, and all of them still fire (precision 1.0).
Small detail: the misses can have activations up to 0.05, slightly above the 0.00-0.02 the explanation states. Not material.
